                                                                             PJM Capacity Market Operations

                                                                                                              Oct. 28, 2026
2028/2029 Base Residual Auction Reserve Target Shortfall
PJM cleared the 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction (BRA) with a reserve margin more than one percentage point
below the Installed Reserve Margin target and with total Unforced Capacity from all Base Load Generation
Resources below the forecasted minimum hourly load. This confirmed shortfall constitutes a triggering event under
the PJM Tariff, requiring an investigation into the root causes of the region's inability to procure sufficient resource
adequacy1.


The 2027/2028 BRA previously triggered these same PJM Tariff provisions, resulting in the publication of the
2027/2028 BRA Shortfall Report, which documented the findings of PJM's investigation. Since the publication of that
report, no significant new information or evidence has emerged that would warrant revisiting or modifying those
findings. Accordingly, the conclusions and recommendations remain unchanged. Readers should refer to the
2027/2028 BRA Shortfall Report for a detailed discussion of the analysis, assumptions, and supporting rationale.
The evaluation of Base Load Generation Resources has been updated below to reflect the results of the 2028/2029
BRA results.


Base Load Generation Resources check
As required in Section 16.3 (a)(ii), Attachment DD of the PJM OATT, PJM will total the committed Unforced Capacity
of all Base Load Generation Resources in a BRA for a Delivery Year and compare that total with the most recent
forecasted minimum hourly load for such Delivery Year. Should a shortfall occur, the Office of the Interconnection will
investigate the cause. If such a shortfall occurs for three consecutive Delivery Years, the Office of the Interconnection
shall declare a capacity shortage and make a filing with FERC for approval to conduct a Reliability Backstop Auction.
Upon receipt of such approval, the Office of the Interconnection will conduct a Reliability Backstop Auction in
accordance with Section 16.4 of the Tariff.


Definition of Base Load Generation Resources
For the purposes of this Reliability Backstop check, PJM determines whether a resource meets the definition of Base
Load status through the following process:

       1 | PJM gathers the most recent 2 full calendar years of hourly performance data submitted to
           GADS by resource owners.

       2 | This data is filtered so that only Nuclear, Combined Cycle and Steam-Coal units are
           considered for Base Load status, as determined by PJM.




1 PJM OATT, Attachment DD § 16.2 and 16.3(a)(ii)

      3 | Applicable units are assigned Base Load status when their operating percentage of available
          Hours exceeds 90%. This is calculated by dividing total service hours by available hours over
          the two-year period. Available hours are any hours when the resource is not on an outage,
          either planned or unplanned. Service hours are defined as hours when the resource is
          synchronized to the grid and providing energy.

      4 | RPM Resources that are classified as Base Load are then compared with the cleared
          Resource List in the BRA to determine total UCAP cleared for each category.
